Generate a Blocked HRF Function (deprecated)

Source: R/hrf.R
gen_hrf_blocked.Rd

gen_hrf_blocked() and its alias hrf_blocked() are deprecated and warn when called. Use block_hrf() to block an existing HRF object, or gen_hrf() with width (e.g. gen_hrf(hrf_gaussian, width = 5)), which is exactly what gen_hrf_blocked() calls.

Usage

gen_hrf_blocked(
  hrf = hrf_gaussian,
  width = 5,
  precision = 0.1,
  half_life = Inf,
  summate = TRUE,
  normalize = FALSE,
  ...
)

hrf_blocked(
  hrf = hrf_gaussian,
  width = 5,
  precision = 0.1,
  half_life = Inf,
  summate = TRUE,
  normalize = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

hrf

A function representing the hemodynamic response function. Default is hrf_gaussian.

width

A numeric value specifying the width of the block in seconds. Default is 5.

precision

A numeric value specifying the sampling resolution in seconds. Default is 0.1.

half_life

A numeric value specifying the half-life of the exponential decay function, used to model response attenuation. Default is Inf, which means no decay.

summate

Logical; if TRUE (default), integrate responses over the block. If FALSE, divide by the block width to obtain a temporal average. Averaging does not fix the peak height: longer blocks can have smaller peaks. Use normalize = TRUE for unit-peak scaling.

normalize

A logical value indicating whether to rescale the output so that the peak of the output is 1. Default is FALSE.

...

Extra arguments passed to the HRF function.

Value

The blocked HRF object returned by gen_hrf().

See also

block_hrf(), gen_hrf()

Examples

# Instead of gen_hrf_blocked(hrf_gaussian, width = 10), use
blocked <- gen_hrf(hrf_gaussian, width = 10)
# or, for an existing HRF object
blocked <- block_hrf(HRF_SPMG1, width = 10)
